I wonder that how do I get a pathdiagram after matrixpls analyisis.
The following is matrixpls script.
------------------------------------------------------

FHE=read.csv("c:/r-SEM/data/FHE.csv")
model<-'A=~a1+a2
R=~r1+r2+r3+r4+r5
H=~h1+h2+h3

H~R'
matrixpls.out<-matrixpls(cov(FHE),model)
summary(matrixpls.out)

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: sempath diagram after matrixpls.
parts:
Hi,

This is not currently possible and although it would not be difficult to implement some kind of support for semPlot that you could use like

semPlot(matrixpls.out)

I do not think that doing so is a good idea for multiple reasons:

1) A path diagram is associated with multiple equations models, but PLS analysis does not do that. Rather, it calculates a set of weighted composites which are then used in separate regression. Presenting these results as a path diagram is likely to mislead your readers.

2) Wold’s original papers (unfortunately) used diagrams that are similar to path diagrams. In these diagrams, the composites were presented as circles, and arrows from indicators to circles were used to indicate that the composite was constructed with “Mode B” and arrows in the other direction were used for “Mode A”. This is problematic again because the reader will interpret the diagram as a factor model or a “formative model”, but that was not the idea in the original diagrams. Moreover, Mode A and Mode B are just a subset of different indicator weighting systems implemented by matrixpls and it is not clear what notation should be used for all the other systems (e.g. principal components.)

3) Some introductory articles misleadingly present PLS as a simultaneous equations technique and present the equations as well. These equations contain the following subset:

eta = beta*eta + zeta
eta = gamma*x + delta

(e.g., Chin, 1998, eq. 1, 7, 9; Fornell & Cha, 1994, eq. 2.16, 2.20, 2.24; Haenlein & Kaplan, 2004; Henseler, Ringle, & Sinkovics, 2009, eq. 1, 3, 5; Tenenhaus, Esposito Vinzi, Chatelin, & Lauro, 2005, pp. 163–166)

The semPlot diagrams do not allow such overlapping equations. But this is a minor problem compared to the fact that under the typical assumption of independent errors (zeta, delta), the model itself is impossible: beta*eta + zeta = gamma*x + delta cannot be true for any population.

4) The purpose of the matrixpls package is to educate people on what PLS does. Providing automatic path diagrams goes against this purpose.


But if you disagree, you can try to convince me otherwise. I understand that some people will consider this a bit off topic. Please let me know and I will start my own email list.  

Mikko
